chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Muhammad ibn al-Haytham al-Tamimi from his father who said:

I performed Hajj with my wife, and she had been bedridden for thirteen years. He said: So when it was night, I placed her on one side of the carrying litter, and I carried her on one side of the litter while the servant carried on the other side. He said: So I performed the obligatory Tawaf with her, and [performed] the Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, and I counted it for myself. Then I met Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and described to him what I had done, and he said, 'It is sufficient for you.'

key_terms.بَيْنَ الصَّفَا وَالْمَرْوَةِ: The Sa'i ritual between the hills of Safa and Marwah
key_terms.شِقِّ مَحْمِلٍ: One side of a carrying litter/sedan chair
key_terms.طَوَافَ الْفَرِيضَةِ: The obligatory circumambulation of the Kaaba
key_terms.قَدْ أَجْزَأَ عَنْكَ: It is sufficient for you / It counts as valid

ai.seo_question: Is it valid to perform Hajj rituals for a bedridden spouse by carrying them on a litter?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *rukhas* (dispensations) in Shia jurisprudence, where physical limitations justify adapting ritual performance without invalidating the act. Imam al-Sadiq’s confirmation that the night-time, assisted Tawaf and Sa'i were sufficient highlights the flexibility of Hajj obligations for those with chronic disabilities, emphasizing ease over rigid formality.
